traits.notes: The seedling exhibits a cluster of simple, obovate leaves with entire margins and pinnate venation. Leaves are arranged alternately along a green, herbaceous stem with fine trichomes. The petiole is short and terete. No stipules, latex, pulvinus, or tendrils are visible. Some minor damage is present on adjacent leaves (not on the subject seedling), but the subject leaves appear intact. The leaf surface is shiny and glabrous, with prominent secondary veins. All images show the same individual from different angles, confirming consistent morphology.

data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (leaves are attached at successive nodes along the stem, alternating sides; no paired or whorled arrangement visible)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves appear grouped near the stem apex, with short internodes)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf has a single blade without leaflets)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (smooth margin with no teeth or serrations visible)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): obovate (wider at the apex and tapering toward the base, with a rounded tip)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): obtuse (rounded or blunt tip)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (base is broadly curved, not tapering or heart-shaped)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (main vein runs from base to apex, with lateral veins branching off and curving toward margin)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, closely spaced, numerous (secondary veins are prominent, forming a reticulate pattern, with many veins per leaf)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (surface appears glossy and reflective, especially in light)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on leaf surface; however, petiole and stem show trichomes)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is relatively short, less than half the leaf blade length)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (circular in cross-section, not flattened or winged)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (stem appears soft and green, not woody)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): present (fine hairs visible along stem, especially in close-up images)
    19. Stem color: green (stem is light to medium green)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (no ridges or lenticels visible; surface appears smooth)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules observed at leaf base)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no exudate or milky sap visible)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joint at leaf base or petiole attachment)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils visible)
F. Notes: The seedling exhibits a cluster of simple, obovate leaves with entire margins and pinnate venation. Leaves are arranged alternately along a green, herbaceous stem with fine trichomes. The petiole is short and terete. No stipules, latex, pulvinus, or tendrils are visible. Some minor damage is present on adjacent leaves (not on the subject seedling), but the subject leaves appear intact. The leaf surface is shiny and glabrous, with prominent secondary veins. All images show the same individual from different angles, confirming consistent morphology.
